items.name: Building height (as published by the architect)
items.note: datum not stated (ground? lowest floor? MSL?). The FAA DOF roof tops are 131/132 ft AGL = 139/140 ft AMSL (ground ~8 ft AMSL); 144 ft matches neither exactly - do NOT use as roof height above ground

conflicting_values.note: "the soaring, 100-foot-high terminal roof" (height above the hall floor, rounded)

items.name: Seismic base isolation
items.note: "the largest building in the world constructed on base isolators" (airportworld25)

items.name: Gates at opening
items.note: SEAONC text via search extract only

items.name: Roof structure
items.value: five sets of steel balanced double-cantilever trusses with a central trussed span, linked into one continuous wing-like form; double-cantilevered trusses linked by bowstring trusses; three-chord "football" trusses

items.name: Roof overall length (published)
items.note: NAIP measures 252.7 m (829 ft) tip to tip (roof.length_obs) - 9 m / 31 ft shorter. Unresolved: possibly measured along the curved top chord or to steel beyond the visible fascia. Concept sketch: 866 ft

items.name: Centre span (between the inner column lines)
End cantilever (outer column line to roof tip)
Double-cantilever truss length
items.value: up to 320

items.name: Central (suspended) section length
items.note: jacked up ~60 ft into place in two phases

items.name: Roof columns
items.note: "supported on 20 cantilevered columns rising from the third floor departures level" (search extract of SEAONC)

items.name: Column grid (concept)
items.value: 40 ft E/W grid by 80 ft N/S column bays
items.note: truss-line spacing confirmed by NAIP (roof.truss_spacing_obs = 12.12 m)

items.name: Roof height above the ticketing hall floor
items.note: "soaring 60 to 90' above the floor of a cavernous ticketing hall" - which surface (top / underside) is not stated

items.name: Glass-enclosed great hall, length x width x height
items.value: 705 x 210 x up to 83
items.note: search engines attribute this sentence to the SEAONC page, which could not be opened. 83 ft is an INTERIOR hall height, not the roof height above ground (the current model js/live/terminals.js uses 83 ft as roof height above ground)

items.name: Bamboo grove height
items.note: "stretches 55 feet high between Levels 2 and 3" (interior)

items.name: Structural rhythm along the axis (tip -> tip)
items.value: 20 ft roof overhang | 140 ft outer truss cantilever | outer column | 80 ft | inner column | 100 ft inner cantilever | 180 ft centre section | 100 | col | 80 | col | 140 | 20
items.method: the only split that satisfies all published numbers at once: 160 (end cantilever) + 80 (column bay) + 380 (centre span) + 80 + 160 = 860; truss 140 + 80 + 100 = 320; centre section 380 - 2 x 100 = 180
items.note: the 20 ft overhang beyond the truss ends is the inferred closure; if the as-built roof is 829 ft (NAIP) the cantilevers or the overhang are ~15 ft shorter each side

items.name: Column lines from the roof centre along the axis
items.note: = +-57.9 m and +-82.3 m. 20 columns = 5 truss lines x 2 double-cantilever trusses x 2 columns (inf; the SOM perspective section shows a column under each truss line)

items.name: Roof axis heading (true north, towards Boarding Area A)
items.method: glazed tip edges and the lens row are perpendicular to the axis; the straight west facade base line confirms it (sd 0.61 m over 182 rows)
items.note: 2.9 deg clockwise from the principal axis of the SFO Museum hall part used by the current model

items.name: Roof centre (relief-corrected, world x/z)
items.method: NAIP roof features moved back by k*h (k = 0.418 at the ITB from DOF poles, h from the eave profile)

items.name: Main roof outline corners (relief-corrected, world x/z)
items.note: rectangle at the eaves; +-1.5 m. Check: DOF roof tops 06-035315/06-035316 fall 1.1 / 0.8 m inside the corrected west eave line

items.name: Roof length tip to tip (fascia to fascia)
items.method: NAIP 0.25 m resampled profile along the axis; imaged 255.25 m, central-projection magnification of an elevated plane removed (H-h = 3633 m from the k(x) slope)
items.note: +-1.5 m; conflicts with the published 860 ft (262.1 m)

items.name: Roof width eave to eave
items.note: +-1.0 m (214 ft); concept sketch 260 ft; published enclosed hall width 210 ft (unverified)

items.name: Truss / skylight lines
items.note: 5 straight glazed lines along the roof ("roof plane is opened with glass along major truss lines", SOM sketch)

items.name: Truss-line spacing
items.method: comb fit of 5 equally spaced lines (north half, 39 rows) and the lens-skylight centres; both 12.25 m imaged
items.note: = 39.8 ft (published grid 40 ft); outer lines 48.5 m apart; outer line to eave ~8.4 m each side

items.name: Centre-section skylights
items.note: lens-shaped (pointed ends) glazed skylights, one per truss line, occupying the central section (published 180 ft = 54.9 m); interior photos show them as glazed basket trusses; +-1 m

items.name: Glazed canopy bands at the two roof tips (depth along the axis)
items.note: bluish glazed grid across the full roof width at both cantilever tips; N/S difference (3 m) not explained; +-1 m

items.name: FAA DOF roof top 06-035315
items.note: AGL 131 ft / AMSL 139 ft, accuracy 1A, verified, JDATE 2013289, 37 36 53.77N 122 23 22.86W -> world (-1258.1, 429.4); lies at the west eave over the column pairs (u = 54.68 m)

items.name: FAA DOF roof top 06-035316
items.note: AGL 132 ft / AMSL 140 ft, accuracy 1A, verified, JDATE 2013289, 37 36 57.35N 122 23 24.26W -> world (-1292.4, 319.1); lies at the west eave over the column pairs (u = -60.86 m)

items.name: Ground elevation at the ITB (from DOF AMSL - AGL)
items.note: 139-131 = 140-132 = 8 ft AMSL (DOF rounding +-1 ft); SFO field elevation 13 ft

items.name: Wing-roof height profile at the west eave (AGL), by distance |u| from the roof centre

centre crown (u ~ 0, glazed centre secti.note: photo only (NAIP cannot see it through the lens glass); +-2 m

items.method: NAIP: the imaged west eave wanders east by 0.955*k*h relative to the straight facade-base line (k = 0.418); even-polynomial fit, RMS 0.20 m in plan; anchored at the peak to the DOF tops. Photo: public-domain frontal photograph, sky/roof silhouette, north/south pair means (perspective not modelled)
items.note: the humps are highest at |u| 67 m, between the inferred inner (57.9 m) and outer (82.3 m) column lines; +-1.5 m below the anchor. The DOF value may belong to the skylight ridges rather than the eave (then all eave values drop by up to ~1-2 m) [unverified]

items.name: Departures level (level 3) floor above ground
items.method: DOF roof top (40.1 m) minus "90 ft" (smith_emery, upper value) = 12.7 m, minus "100 ft" (sfgate2000) = 9.6 m; midpoint
items.note: +-1.5 m; no drawing or survey found - see open questions

items.name: West (landside, front) wall
items.value: full-height glass wall, glass with three layers of ceramic frit ("like a scrim"); concept sketch: bands of translucent patterned frit, clear glass and translucent glass / metal brise-soleil
items.note: photos: lower band clear glazing at the curb with entrance vestibules and a canopy; upper wall light fritted panels; pairs of white columns at the column lines; roof trusses exposed above the wall

items.name: North and south end walls
items.value: custom unitized curtain walls spanning over 60 ft (vertical exterior end walls under the roof)

items.name: Hall back (east) wall, interior
items.value: cherry-wood clad high wall

items.name: Roof and envelope upgrade 2024-2026
items.value: new roof membrane and waterproofing, ~1,400 kW rooftop PV, expansion joints, window-washing (facade access) system, curtain-wall mullion caps, exposed-steel corrosion repair; west facade scaffolded in four phases; ceremony 2024-06-27, completion early/mid 2026
items.note: NAIP 2024 (2024-05-20) predates the works: the 2026 roof carries PV arrays whose layout is not documented in any open source found (open question)

items.name: NAIP 2024 relief displacement factor near the ITB

value.model: k(x) = a + b*x (x = world east of the object foot, m)

items.note: 5 DOF poles 153-157 ft AGL; scatter 0.0022; k at ITB roof 0.418; predicts the tower cab lean (38-40 m) for 69-73 m height vs DOF top 74.7 m (245 ft incl. appurtenances)

items.name: Sun at the NAIP 2024 exposure near the ITB
items.note: shadow of DOF pole 06-034826 (108 ft): azimuth ~187 deg, elevation ~72.4 deg (the local-noon maximum for 2024-05-20) - for later shadow checks

items.name: Architect / builder
items.value: Gerson/Overstreet Architects; built by Hensel Phelps Construction
items.note: secondary (Wikipedia citing the 2007 flySFO fact sheet)

items.name: Gates
items.note: AGS: 23 passenger boarding bridges at A1-A15 reconfigured (completed 2020); A6 retrofitted for a three-bridge A380 operation (AGS) - Wikipedia names A11 for three jetways (conflict, gate-level detail)

items.name: Footprint
items.value: SFO Museum polygon (data/sfo_airport.json "Boarding Area A"): 339 m along the pier axis incl. the connector; body width 38.7-38.8 m
items.note: NAIP imaged roof (fascia to fascia) 36.5 m at three stations (by eye, +-1 m); the SFO Museum edge includes the oblique facade band

items.name: Main pier roof height above apron
items.method: (a) NAIP west-side dark band (oblique WNW facade + shadow) 8.5-9 m wide = (0.873 k + 0.122) h with k = 0.42 -> 17.4-18.4 m (minus any roof overhang); (b) NAIP roof centre vs SFO Museum footprint centre 5.85 m = 0.873 k h -> 15.9 m
items.note: +-2.5 m. Consistent with a three-level pier (apron + two passenger levels) [inf]. OSM says 25 m (unsourced)

items.name: Raised roof pods
items.note: by eye on NAIP (+-3 m); the first pod (nearest the ITB) top is FAA DOF 06-035352 = 85 ft AGL (25.9 m, 94 ft AMSL); its oblique rim band (2.5-3 m) gives ~7.5 m above the main roof, consistent with 17 + 7.5 = 24.5-26 m

items.name: FAA DOF 06-035352
items.note: BLDG 85 ft AGL / 94 ft AMSL, 1A, 37 36 49.70N 122 23 20.30W -> world (-1195.3, 555.0): west side of Boarding Area A pod 1 (pier frame u ~ -125 m)

items.name: Architect / builder
items.value: Robin Chiang & Company (Tutor Perini page); Wikipedia: Hellmuth, Obata + Kassabaum with Robin Chiang & Company and Robert B. Wong Architects; built by Tutor Perini; completed 1999; contract $95 M

items.name: Stories / levels
items.value: three-story: apron level (airline operations, storage, MEP); level 2 international arrivals, sterile corridor, clubs, in-transit lounge with gate-room access; level 3 departures concourse with retail

items.name: Gate rooms
items.value: six double-gated, two-level common-use gate rooms for twelve 747-400s

items.name: Exterior
items.value: metallic-finish composite aluminium panels and a tinted energy-efficient glazed curtain wall

items.name: Footprint
items.value: SFO Museum polygon (data/sfo_airport.json "Boarding Area G"): body width 38.3-38.4 m, 47 m at the middle pod
items.note: NAIP imaged roof width ~33.5 m by eye (edges ambiguous, low); the SFO Museum G outline is offset ~3-6 m NNE of the relief-corrected NAIP roof (imagery.md s.6 lists +4 m) - unresolved

items.name: Main pier roof height above apron
items.method: NAIP: NNE shadow band + SSW oblique facade band = 4.5-5.5 m = 0.297 h (sun elevation 72.4 deg, azimuth 187 deg; k = 0.36)
items.note: +-3 m; three-story (pub) supports ~17-20 m [inf]

items.name: Raised roof pods
items.note: by eye on NAIP (+-3 m); heights not measured - no DOF entry on Boarding Area G

items.name: RADP projects touching the ITB (2019 NOP)
items.value: Main Hall western expansion of levels 2-3 (~140,000 sq ft, 70,000 per level); Boarding Areas A (+10,800 sq ft) and G (+12,400 sq ft) "bump-outs"; ITB curbside expansion; Boarding Area H connected through the ITB
items.note: planning-stage only; whether any was built by 2026 is not verified

current_model_deviations: js/live/terminals.js greatHall(): roof top at 83 ft (25.3 m) above ground; the DOF roof tops are 131/132 ft AGL (40 m) - 83 ft is the (unverified) interior hall height
greatHall(): roof length 380 + 2x160 + 2x12 ft ~ 237 m and width 210 ft + 18 m ~ 82 m; NAIP: 252.7 m x 65.4 m (published 860 ft long)
greatHall(): placed on the SFO Museum hall part axis/centre; the roof axis is rotated 2.9 deg (heading 162.85) and its centre is [-1245.03, 364.7]
greatHall(): 20 columns as 2 x 10 along the long edges; published/inferred: 5 truss lines x 4 columns at +-190 / +-270 ft along the axis

greatHall(): roof top profile highest over the column lines and lower at centre/tips - matches qualitatively, but the centre crown (glazed lens section) rises again to ~the hump height and the notches between wings and centre are ~5 m lower
data/sfo_buildings.json: Boarding Areas A/G at 14.6 m; NAIP relief/shadow gives ~17 m (+-2.5/3 m) plus pods to ~26 m (A pod 1: DOF 85 ft)
unverified: flySFO "Fact Sheet - International Terminal" (2007) could not be retrieved (web.archive.org refused); its dimensions are only known through Wikipedia
AISC Modern Steel Construction Feb 2000 article and the SEAONC Legacy page: only search-engine extracts could be read (bot challenges)
the "705 x 210 x 83 ft" great-hall figures: attribution to SEAONC not confirmed first-hand
datum of the architect's "144 ft" building height
departures (level 3) floor elevation above ground (inferred 11.5 +-1.5 m)
roof tip and centre-crown heights (NAIP + one photo, +-1.5-2 m); whether the DOF tops are the eave or skylight ridges
as-built roof length: NAIP 252.7 m vs published 860 ft (262.1 m)
pier roof heights (NAIP relief/shadow only), heights of pods other than A pod 1, G pod heights
post-2024 roof: PV array layout, new membrane colour
gate with the three-bridge A380 operation: A6 (AGS) vs A11 (Wikipedia)
open_questions: Owner: can we obtain SFO / SF Planning / SOM drawings (sections, elevations) of the ITB? e.g. SFO Bureau of Design and Construction record drawings, or the 1992 SFO Master Plan FEIR (the ITB EIR) - they would fix the level heights and the roof profile
Which length to model: NAIP 252.7 m (as imaged) or the published 860 ft? Proposed: NAIP for the planform, published rhythm scaled to it, flagged on the drawing
Roof appearance for 2026: new membrane + 1.4 MW PV - needs post-2024 imagery (NAIP 2026 when released, or owner photos); until then model the 2024 roof
Pier heights: accept the NAIP-derived ~17 m (with pods ~26 m) or wait for an elevation source?
Boarding Area G outline: SFO Museum polygon offset vs NAIP - retrace from NAIP ground-level edges?
